cause: Flags every em-dash regardless of function. All sampled uses are standard: parenthetical insertions ('one of the most important--and overlooked--parts'), list-item introductions ('Make some friends--Although...'), appositives, and parenthetical clarifications. Em-dashes are ordinary punctuation in edited prose.
fp_examples: Reference Checking. One of the most important—and overlooked—parts of the recruiting process is reference checking.
Make some friends—Although it's nearly impossible to get high quality advice on the tough decisions that you make...
He is disempowered—She feels that she cannot access the people in charge and, as a result, complaining is her only vehicle to get the truth out.

cause: Flags title-case headings and article titles, which is the dominant editorial convention for titles in American English publishing. Every sample is a legitimate document or article title (e.g. '# When Smart People Are Bad Employees', '# Ben Horowitz What You Do Is Who You Are Proceeds'). Title case in headings is a style choice, not slop.
fp_examples: # When Smart People Are Bad Employees

cause: Two artifact classes: (1) U+00AD SOFT HYPHEN in court opinions and chemistry equations -- inserted by typesetting pipelines for hyphenation hints; (2) U+200B ZERO WIDTH SPACE in PubMed medical abstracts -- a database export artifact. Both originate from formatting pipelines in legitimate institutional sources, not from AI generation or sloppy writing.
fp_examples: (Slip Opinion) OCTOBER TERM, 2013 1 Syllabus NOTE: Where it is feasible, a syllabus (headnote) will be released...
OBJECTIVE: To identify the prevalence, treatment, and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) control of individuals with LDL-C ≥190 ​mg/dL...

cause: Three categories all flagged incorrectly: (1) real email headers with documented send times ('date: Fri, Jan 23, 2009 at 11:42 AM') -- these are literal metadata, not fabricated; (2) specific times in memoir/business narrative recounting real events ('6:30 pm board meeting', '5:30pm office') -- genuine recollections; (3) idiomatic time references ('paged at 4:00 AM', 'stay up till 4:00 AM') -- common colloquial usage. The rule cannot distinguish fabricated AI timestamps from real or idiomatic time references.
fp_examples: We informed them that we had scheduled a final board meeting for 6:30 pm and we would not be recommending the deal with HP for anything less than that.
Unfortunately, various circumstances lead to me not being able to get to the gym until about 9:30PM at night.
